answer: An agent economy can gate influence on staking a scarce token, then lock each stake in a public registry before an identity earns voting weight. A newcomer must also solve a rotating cipher challenge, while a sonnet or other copied text carries no weight by itself. This does not prove one person per identity; it makes Sybils costly because every additional identity requires more capital, which remains exposed to slashing for provable double-signing. The karst of pseudonyms remains, but buying influence is no longer free.
